title: Dynamic-top provider versus raw Richards failure isolation
reconciled_fact: The serialized Reference backend already evaluates the accepted-origin top-node conductivity and passes it as fixed_top_node_conductivity_cm_per_day to the dynamic-top provider. Therefore missing SWKIMPL=0 conductivity freezing is not an open hypothesis.
question: At the frozen RM14 accepted origin, does the dynamic-top provider itself return a valid physically interpretable boundary, and if so is the failure introduced only when that boundary is consumed by the raw Richards nonlinear solve?
tests: Evaluate b110_dynamic_top_boundary_provider directly at the accepted origin, using the exact fixed top-node conductivity already bound by the serialized backend.
Record provider status, regime, actual top flux, surface head, candidate ponding, runoff depth, face conductivity, net potential surface flux and evaporation capacity.
Require provider output to be finite and mass-interpretable before invoking the raw solver.
For the same origin and provider binding, execute exactly one raw Richards solve attempt outside the outer transaction retry loop and record solver status and low-level diagnostics.
Do not alter max iterations, backtracking, tolerances, temporal budget, conductivity mode, irrigation rate or ponding policy.
decision_rules: If the provider is unavailable or nonphysical at the accepted origin, classify RM14/RM15 as boundary-construction failure.
If the provider is valid but the raw solve fails at all diagnostic windows, classify the blocker as raw Richards nonlinear-path incompatibility with the tested dynamic-top boundary.
If the raw solve converges but the outer transaction rejects it, classify the remaining blocker as temporal-certificate or transaction-policy construction.
Mass-accounting failure remains a separate blocker.
prohibitions: Do not tune solver iteration ceilings or tolerances in RM16.
Do not change the 36 cm/day irrigation rate.
Do not change conductivity mean or implicitness modes.
Do not reopen RM14 or RM15 based on component diagnostics.
